analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, patches and all supplied BASE/HEAD text against the canonical definition index and selected boundary details. The changes document release extraction using /usr/bin/tar under umask 022 (changelog.d/installer-release-file-modes.md:3; docs/operations/provider-release.md:411–414) and update the documentation date. No executable implementation is supplied in this batch, so these statements do not establish actual permission enforcement or a regression. Wider readability of public release artifacts is not itself exposure of A-001, A-003 or A-008, nor does umask 022 itself confer write access to other users. The existing production signing requirement, prerelease exception and separation of release identity from serving permission remain unchanged, consistent with T-013, T-054, TB-002 and TB-011. No changed authorization, encryption, billing, cache, media or privileged-helper control is evidenced here.
Integration must examine scripts/install.sh, particularly install_bundle_atomically: confirm the umask override is scoped to release extraction, cannot affect later credential/private-state creation, and preserves signature/hash verification and safe staging before installation. Check actual archive modes and resulting writable paths rather than treating this documentation as proof that installed files or private state have safe permissions. This is a material implementation coverage limit, not an observed missing control; no finding is supported by the documentation-only evidence.
